statement.p: (a) Let \mbox{div }\vec F=x^2+y^2+z^2+8. Calculate \int_{S_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec A where S_1 is the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin.

(b) Let S_2 be the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin; let S_3 be the sphere of radius 4 centered at the origin; let S_4 be the box of side 4 centered at the origin with edges parallel to the axes. Without calculating them, arrange the following integrals in increasing order: A = \int_{S_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec A,\quad B = \int_{S_3}\vec F\cdot d\vec A, \quad C = \int_{S_4}\vec F\cdot d\vec A.

static.solution:
(a) Let W_1 be the ball inside S_1. By the Divergence Theorem, \int_{S_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec A=\int_{W_1}(x^2+y^2+z^2+8)\,dV. Using spherical coordinates, we have \int_{S_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\int_0^{1}(\rho^2+8)\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta = 2\pi \cdot \left.\left(\frac{\rho^5}5+\frac{8}{3}\rho^3\right)\right|_0^1(-\cos\phi)\bigg|_0^{\pi} = \frac{172\pi}{15}
(b) If we were to calculate all three integrals using the Divergence Theorem, we would be integrating \mbox{div }\vec F through the interior of each of these regions. Since S_2 lies entirely inside S_{4}, and S_{4} lies entirely inside S_{3}, and since \mbox{div }\vec F=x^2+y^2+z^2+8 is positive everywhere, \int_{S_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec A \lt \int_{S_{4}}\vec F\cdot d\vec A\lt \int_{S_{3}}\vec F\cdot d\vec A.
